criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear benefit to Australia and users identified with good rationale and literature links, but goals/objectives/requirements lack specific engineering detail and referencing is bare URLs.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict
In 2016, a bleaching killed 30 percent of the reef’s coral.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Detailed Gantt Wk2-Wk10 with task descriptions, deadlines, buffer Week 10, and Useful Links. Covers launch, orbit, ground, comms, EOL and STK, fitting mission narrative; contingency only implicit.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: No calculations, orbit parameters, or STK outputs shown. Only claims of background reading and tutorials. No interpretable technical results to demonstrate progress.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Readable structure with headings and Gantt, but figure unc captioned, references are bare URLs not proper citations, and writing has awkward phrasing.

evidence.quote: Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.

technical_issues.issue: No quantified mission requirements: resolution, revisit, coverage, latency, SST accuracy.
No orbit calculations, COEs/AOEs, launch trade, link budget or STK plots presented.
Gantt chart has no figure number, caption or axis legend in text.
References are bare URLs without author, date, title; in-text superscripts do not match Useful Links list.

overall: Promising reef-monitoring concept with feasible plan and STK choice, but almost no demonstrated technical design work yet; needs quantitative requirements and early orbit/STK results.

feedback.summary: You proposed a promising reef-monitoring mission with clear users and a feasible Wk2-Wk10 plan using STK. Your next gains are to quantify mission requirements, show early orbit and STK results, and tidy figures and references to lift presentation.
next_steps: In Mission Concept & Rationale, add quantified requirements for resolution, revisit, coverage, latency and SST accuracy for your near-real-time relay to monitoring stations.
In Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, add first technical results with brief interpretation such as orbit calculations, COEs/AOEs, launch trade, link budget or STK plots.
Number and caption Image 1 Gantt with axis legend, and convert Useful Links bare URLs to proper citations that match your in-text superscripts.

criteria.C1: You made a clear case in Mission Concept & Rationale for reef monitoring for marine and conservation scientists, including your near-real-time relay idea and 2016 bleaching context. To reach Accomplished, you need quantified requirements for resolution, revisit, coverage, latency and SST accuracy, and replace bare URLs with proper in-text literature references.
criteria.C2: You built a strong Project Plan & Preliminary Progress with your Wk2-Wk10 Gantt, task descriptions, Week 10 buffer and Useful Links covering launch, orbit, ground, comms, EOL and STK. To stay securely at Accomplished, make your contingency explicit for variations and explain why each phase follows from your mission narrative.
criteria.C3: You showed initiative in Project Plan & Preliminary Progress by completing STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4. To move to Adequate and beyond, you must show interpretable technical results with brief description, such as initial orbit calculations, COEs/AOEs, launch trade, link budget or STK plots.
criteria.C4: You presented a readable report with headings and your Image 1 Gantt in Project Plan & Preliminary Progress. To reach Accomplished, you need to add figure number, caption and axis legend, format Useful Links as proper author-date-title citations matching in-text superscripts, and polish awkward phrasing.
